meta.title: Dojo | Train how you work with AI agents
meta.description: Build better habits with AI coding agents through real work, reflection and practice.

HomePage.title: Train how you work with AI agents.
HomePage.description: Dojo is being built to help developers improve how they work with AI coding agents through real work, reflection, skill development and practice.

promptClarity.name: Prompt clarity
promptClarity.summary: Whether a request says what to do, where, within what limits, and how done looks.

planning.name: Planning before coding
planning.summary: Whether larger builds start from a plan, a requirements list or named edge cases.

verification.name: Verifying AI output
verification.summary: Whether delivered work is tested, checked or questioned before moving on.

iteration.name: Iteration quality
iteration.summary: Whether follow-ups give the agent something new and specific to act on.

scopeControl.name: Scope control
scopeControl.summary: Whether requests name their targets and limits instead of sweeping wide.

statesGoal.label: States the task
statesGoal.shows: Names the action and what it applies to.
statesGoal.missing: The request doesn't say what should happen.
statesGoal.why: An agent can only aim at a goal it can read.
statesGoal.practice: Open with one sentence: the action and its target.

givesContext.label: Gives concrete context
givesContext.shows: Points at something specific: a file, route, identifier or error.
givesContext.missing: Nothing specific is named, so the agent has to guess where to look.
givesContext.why: Concrete anchors stop the agent searching, or inventing, what you meant.
givesContext.practice: Name the file, page, function or exact error message.

statesConstraints.label: States constraints
statesConstraints.shows: Says what must, or must not, change.
statesConstraints.missing: A larger request with no limits stated.
statesConstraints.why: Without limits, an agent fills the gaps with its own assumptions.
statesConstraints.practice: Add one line: what must not change.

definesDone.label: Defines done
definesDone.shows: Describes the result the work will be checked against.
definesDone.missing: A larger request with no description of the finished result.
definesDone.why: A stated outcome is what you and the agent both check the work against.
definesDone.practice: Add "Done when…" with something you can observe.

vagueReference.label: Vague reference
vagueReference.shows: Refers to "it" or "this" without naming it.
vagueReference.missing: Refers to "it" or "this" without saying what that is.
vagueReference.why: The agent resolves "it" from its own context, which may not be yours.
vagueReference.practice: Replace "it" with the name of the thing.

asksForPlan.label: Plans before building
asksForPlan.shows: Asks for a plan, analysis or options before any code.
asksForPlan.missing: No plan was asked for before the build.
asksForPlan.why: Reviewing a plan is cheaper than reviewing a wrong implementation.
asksForPlan.practice: Ask for a plan first, and approve it before any code is written.

structuredRequirements.label: Structured requirements
structuredRequirements.shows: Lays the work out as a list of requirements or steps.
structuredRequirements.missing: The requirements arrived as one block of prose.
structuredRequirements.why: A list makes each requirement checkable on its own.
structuredRequirements.practice: Put the requirements in a numbered list.

considersEdgeCases.label: Considers edge cases
considersEdgeCases.shows: Raises failure cases or limits up front.
considersEdgeCases.missing: No failure cases or limits were raised.
considersEdgeCases.why: Edge cases named up front are handled in the first version, not found later.
considersEdgeCases.practice: Name two ways the feature could fail.

straightToBuild.label: Straight to building
straightToBuild.shows: A larger build started with no plan.
straightToBuild.missing: A larger build was requested with no plan, requirements list or edge cases first.
straightToBuild.why: Without a plan, the first review is of finished code, when changes cost the most.
straightToBuild.practice: Ask for a plan first, and approve it before any code is written.

asksForVerification.label: Asks for verification
asksForVerification.shows: Asks for tests, checks or proof as part of the work.
asksForVerification.missing: The request did not ask for any check.
asksForVerification.why: Asking for proof up front makes checking part of the work, not an afterthought.
asksForVerification.practice: End larger requests with how the result should be checked.

checksResult.label: Checks the result
checksResult.shows: Follows up by testing, checking, or reporting what actually happened.
checksResult.why: A change is done when it is seen to work, not when the agent says so.
checksResult.practice: Run it, then tell the agent what you saw.

challengesClaims.label: Challenges claims
challengesClaims.shows: Questions the agent's claims, or asks how it knows.
challengesClaims.missing: The agent's claims were taken as given.
challengesClaims.why: Agents state results confidently whether or not they checked them.
challengesClaims.practice: Ask "how did you verify that?" before moving on.

acceptedWithoutCheck.label: Moved on without checking
acceptedWithoutCheck.shows: Work was delivered and the next prompts moved on.
acceptedWithoutCheck.missing: Work was delivered, and the next prompts moved on without a check.
acceptedWithoutCheck.why: An unchecked change becomes the foundation for the next one.
acceptedWithoutCheck.practice: Before the next task, ask for the test output, or check it yourself and say what you saw.

specificFeedback.label: Specific feedback
specificFeedback.shows: The follow-up includes the exact error, output, file or value.
specificFeedback.why: The agent can only fix what it can see.
specificFeedback.practice: Paste the exact error or output.

statesExpectedVsActual.label: Expected versus actual
statesExpectedVsActual.shows: Says what was expected and what happened instead.
statesExpectedVsActual.missing: The follow-up did not say what was expected.
statesExpectedVsActual.why: The gap between expected and actual is the bug report.
statesExpectedVsActual.practice: Write one line each: what you expected, what happened.

refinesRequirement.label: Refines the request
refinesRequirement.shows: Adjusts the requirement in light of the result.
refinesRequirement.why: Changing the requirement directly beats repeating the old one.
refinesRequirement.practice: Say what to change, starting with "Instead…".

vagueFeedback.label: Vague feedback
vagueFeedback.shows: Says something is wrong without saying what.
vagueFeedback.missing: Says something is wrong without saying what.
vagueFeedback.why: The agent has to guess at the problem, and often guesses a different one.
vagueFeedback.practice: Paste the error or output, and say what you expected.

repeatedPrompt.label: Repeated prompt
repeatedPrompt.shows: Sends nearly the same prompt again.
repeatedPrompt.missing: Sends nearly the same prompt again.
repeatedPrompt.why: The same prompt tends to produce the same answer.
repeatedPrompt.practice: If a prompt didn't work, change it: add what went wrong.

namesTargets.label: Names its targets
namesTargets.shows: Names the files, routes or components in play.
namesTargets.missing: No file, route or component was named.
namesTargets.why: Named targets keep the change where you want it.
namesTargets.practice: Name the file or component the change belongs in.

setsBoundaries.label: Sets boundaries
setsBoundaries.shows: Limits the change: only this, not that.
setsBoundaries.missing: Nothing was ruled out of the change.
setsBoundaries.why: Boundaries stop an agent "improving" things you did not ask about.

broadRequest.label: Broad request
broadRequest.shows: Asks for sweeping change: everything, the whole app, from scratch.
broadRequest.missing: Asks for sweeping change: everything, the whole app, from scratch.
broadRequest.why: Sweeping requests produce sweeping diffs that are hard to review.
broadRequest.practice: Split it: one component or one behaviour per request.

bundledRequest.label: Several tasks at once
bundledRequest.shows: Bundles many separate tasks into one prompt.
bundledRequest.missing: Bundles many separate tasks into one prompt.
bundledRequest.why: Bundled tasks are done unevenly, and are hard to check one by one.
bundledRequest.practice: Send one task, check it, then send the next.

privacy.heading: What Dojo stores

items.parsed: Your prompts and the agent's answers, parsed from each log and redacted.
items.metrics: The free metrics of each upload, as calculated when it was saved.
items.assessments: Every rubric assessment, with its scores, evidence and recommendations.
items.account: Your email address and your sign-in, held by Supabase Auth.
items.rawFiles: The raw log files you choose. They are read in your browser and never uploaded.
items.secrets: Credentials the redactor recognises: keys, tokens, passwords in URLs, auth headers.
items.identity: The author name, email and GitHub login recorded in a log's header.
items.thirdParties: Nothing is sent to an AI provider. Scoring runs on Dojo's own server, by rules.

privacy.redaction: Redaction recognises common credential formats. It cannot recognise every secret, and it does not remove names, private code or file paths. Avoid pasting secrets into agent sessions in the first place.

delete.heading: Delete your account
delete.body: This deletes every upload, session, metric and assessment in your workspace, then your sign-in. It cannot be undone.
